mainTopic: Where on the windpipe a valid שחיטה may be done, and how cuts partly out of place (מוגרמת) are judged
overview: The גמרא rules that a שחיטה from the שיפוי כובע (the slope of the thyroid cartilage) and below is valid. רב חנן בר רב קטינא challenges רב נחמן, who ruled this way, because the ruling seems to match neither רבנן nor רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. רב נחמן answers that he relies on a received teaching, not on either side's reasoning. Next, רבי יהושע בן לוי sets out three levels of leniency for a cut that slipped too high (מוגרמת): רבנן, then רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, then רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס. The הלכה follows רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, as רב נחמן did. The גמרא then asks exactly which cut of thirds רבנן and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה argue about: two-thirds properly and then one-third out of place, or the reverse. רב הונא and רב חסדא disagree, and the גמרא brings two versions of their debate, including a challenge to the proof from the משנה 'רובו של אחד כמוהו'. Last, the גמרא discusses three-part cuts, with רב הונא and רב יהודה reporting opposite rulings in the name of רב. רב חסדא tells רב הונא not to take back his ruling, and the reason comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The final halacha: cutting from the slope of the thyroid cartilage and below is valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that שחיטה from the שיפוי כובע and below is valid, because some of the חיטי are still left above the cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: if he slaughtered from the downward slope of the thyroid cartilage and below, it is valid. That is the case where he left over some of the arytenoid cartilage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical bottom line about how high on the windpipe one may cut. Starting from the place where the thyroid cartilage begins to slope downward is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שיפוי כובע is the sloping part of the large cartilage at the top of the windpipe. Cutting there is valid because some of the חיטי (the small grain-shaped cartilages) are still left above the cut. So this ruling matches the view that leaving part of the חיטי still allows a valid שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: The halacha, the practical ruling
The downward slope of the 'hat', meaning the thyroid cartilage at the top of the windpipe
Valid; the animal is kosher
The arytenoid cartilages, small bumps shaped like grains of wheat
Left over

steps.whatToRemember: הלכה: a שחיטה from the שיפוי כובע and below is valid.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical upper limit on the windpipe for a valid שחיטה.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: from the incline of the thyroid cartilage and below, it is valid,
phrases.notes: The 'כובע' (literally 'hat') is the large cartilage at the top of the windpipe, and שיפוי is where it slopes down.

phrases.english: and that is where he left over some of the arytenoid cartilage.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא מִשִּׁיפּוּי כּוֹבַע וּלְמַטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion (from the previous section) about the upper limit of the place of שחיטה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Cutting from the שיפוי כובע and below is valid, since part of the חיטי remains above the cut.

steps.title: רב נחמן rules the slaughter valid from the slope and below
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן put the halacha into practice and declared a שחיטה valid when it was done from the שיפוי כובע and below.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן declared valid a slaughter done from the incline of the thyroid cartilage and below.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story of רב נחמן ruling in a real case, using the same rule as the הלכה above. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same ruling as Step 1, now shown as an actual decision of רב נחמן. The question it raises is which earlier opinion this ruling is based on.

keyTerms.meaning: Declared valid / kosher

phrases.english: Rav Nachman declared valid
a slaughter from the incline of the thyroid cartilage and below.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אַכְשַׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the ruling of Step 1 applied in practice by רב נחמן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן ruled that slaughter from the שיפוי כובע and below is valid.

steps.title: Whose opinion is this? It fits neither side
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן בר רב קטינא asks רב נחמן which opinion his ruling follows, since it seems to match neither רבנן nor רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנן בר רב קטינא said to רב נחמן: According to whom are you ruling? Not according to רבנן and not according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנן בר רב קטינא challenges רב נחמן's ruling. He says it does not match either of the known opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the earlier discussion, both רבנן and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה hold that cutting the windpipe above the large upper ring is not valid. The שיפוי כובע is even higher than that ring. So רב נחמן's ruling seems to go beyond what either side allows.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? (which opinion does this follow)
The Rabbis, the majority opinion

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חָנָן בַּר רַב קַטִּינָא לְרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Chanan bar Rav Ketina said to Rav Nachman:
In accordance with whom?

phrases.aramaic: לָא כְּרַבָּנַן וְלָא כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: Not like the Rabbis and not like Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן? לָא כְּרַבָּנַן וְלָא כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of רב נחמן in Step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that cutting from the שיפוי כובע and below is valid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both known opinions require the cut to be at or below the large ring. A cut higher up, at the שיפוי כובע, should then be invalid according to everyone.

steps.title: רב נחמן relies on a received teaching
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that he is not relying on the reasoning of either side. He has a received teaching that a cut from the שיפוי כובע and below is valid. It is reported in the name of רבי יוחנן, or רבי חנינא, or רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I don't know חילק and I don't know בילק. I know a received teaching. As רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן; and some say רבי אבא בר זבדא said in the name of רבי חנינא; and some say רבי יעקב בר אידי said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: from the slope of the thyroid cartilage and below, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends himself. He is not basing his ruling on רבנן or רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. He is basing it on a direct teaching he received.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'I don't know חילק or בילק,' רב נחמן is saying he is not trying to fit this ruling into either side's opinion. A received teaching (שמעתא) is enough to rule on, even if it doesn't fit neatly into either opinion. The teaching comes with three possible chains of transmission, all ending in the same rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Chilak and Bilak': a way of saying 'this one and that one', meaning neither side's reasoning
A received teaching passed down from earlier teachers
I know

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not saying the two sides are wrong. He is saying his ruling does not depend on their reasoning, because he has a direct tradition.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a clear received teaching can decide the הלכה even when it doesn't fit any known opinion.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא לָא חִילָק יָדַעְנָא
phrases.english: He said to him: I do not know Chilak
phrases.notes: חילק and בילק sound like made-up names, like saying 'this guy and that guy'. He means he isn't following either side's reasoning.

phrases.english: and I do not know Bilak;
I know the received teaching,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: as Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא,
phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Abba bar Zavda said in the name of Rabbi Chanina,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לָהּ אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי
phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi said
in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
from the incline of the thyroid cartilage and below, it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנָא לָא חִילָק יָדַעְנָא וְלָא בִּילָק יָדַעְנָא, אֲנָא שְׁמַעְתָּא יָדַעְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Appeal to a received tradition instead of to either side's reasoning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The questioner assumed every ruling must match either רבנן or רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling stands on a received teaching (attributed to רבי יוחנן, רבי חנינא, or רבי יהושע בן לוי, depending on the version), so it does not need to match either opinion.

steps.title: What רבנן call a diverted cut is valid for רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that a cut which רבנן call מוגרמת (out of place) would be valid according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: The diverted cut of the רבנן is valid according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement of רבי יהושע בן לוי. It compares how the two earlier opinions treat a cut that slipped too high.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מוגרמת is a cut where the knife slipped upward, out of the proper place, above the ring. רבנן say such a cut is invalid. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה allows the cut when most of the windpipe was cut within the large upper ring, so the same case would be valid according to him.

keyTerms.meaning: A diverted cut: the knife slipped upward out of the proper place of שחיטה
Of the Rabbis; here, the case the Rabbis call מוגרמת

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean רבנן hold this cut is valid. It is the case that רבנן call מוגרמת and disqualify, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה would allow it.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The diverted cut of the Rabbis,
is valid according to Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: מוּגְרֶמֶת דְּרַבָּנַן כְּשֵׁרָה לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the earlier discussion of רבנן and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, adding a new statement of רבי יהושע בן לוי, who was also quoted in Step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cut that רבנן disqualify as מוגרמת is valid according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.

steps.title: The second half of the teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.stepSummary: A cut that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה calls out of place would be valid according to רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a cut that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה calls out of place is valid according to רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי finishes his teaching. He adds one more rung to the ladder: what רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה disqualifies, רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס allows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three levels here. רבנן are the strictest, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה is more lenient, and רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס is the most lenient. Each one allows a cut that the stricter opinion calls out of place.

keyTerms.meaning: Valid; the שחיטה works and the animal may be eaten.

phrases.english: And the [out-of-place cut] of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda
phrases.notes: The word 'out of place' (מוגרמת) is carried over from the first half of this teaching.

phrases.english: is valid according to Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּדְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה כְּשֵׁרָה לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the statement that began in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: What רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה calls מוגרמת is still כשרה for רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהושע בן לוי needed to say this.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second half of the teaching as obvious, so why say it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows that רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס is the most lenient. So it seems clear without being told that he would allow what רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה forbids.

keyTerms.meaning: It's obvious; why does this need to be said?

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second half of the teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס is the most lenient, his allowing this is self-evident, so the statement adds nothing.

steps.title: We might have thought he only answers רבנן
steps.stepSummary: Without this teaching we might think רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס was only arguing with רבנן and actually agrees with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס is responding to רבנן. So it teaches us that he is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the teaching is needed. It blocks a mistaken reading of how far רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס was only disagreeing with רבנן and stopped at the position of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that he goes further, so he really is a separate, more lenient opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said; this sets up the mistake the teaching comes to prevent.
Literally 'stands on'; here it means 'is responding to'.
It teaches us (something new).

phrases.english: You might have said:
Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus
is responding to the Rabbis,
so it teaches us [that this is not so].

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the statement prevents a mistaken reading (מהו דתימא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס only disagrees with רבנן and agrees with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: He goes beyond רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה and allows even his out-of-place cut.

steps.title: Maybe that mistaken reading is right
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: why not say that רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס really does agree with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה?
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that it really is so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. Maybe the 'mistaken' reading is actually correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 8 assumed that reading was wrong. Now the גמרא asks what proves it wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: But say it really is so; this challenges an assumption.

phrases.english: But say that it really is so!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא הָכִי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס goes beyond רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing has yet shown that he does not simply agree with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.

steps.title: The wording 'testified' proves he stands alone
steps.stepSummary: If he agreed with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, the text would say 'he testified about it'. Since it says only 'testified', he holds his own view.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it should have said 'he testified about it'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves its point from the exact wording used for רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Had he simply been backing up רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, the text would say he testified 'about it', meaning about that view. Because it just says he testified, his is an independent opinion, more lenient than both.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; it introduces what would follow from the other side's claim.
He testified about it, meaning he supported that view.
It should have said.

phrases.english: If so,
it should have said, 'he testified about it.'
phrases.notes: The text only says 'he testified', without 'about it', so he isn't just backing up another view.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן הֵעִיד עָלֶיהָ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס agrees with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The plain word 'testified' shows he holds his own, more lenient view.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, because רב נחמן acted that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is like רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, since רב נחמן holds like him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling. The הלכה follows the most lenient opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's practical ruling in step 2 matches רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס. That ruling allowed a cut from the שיפוי כובע and below. So the הלכה follows him.

keyTerms.meaning: And the halacha is like ...
Like him, in agreement with him.

steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels of leniency: רבנן, then רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, then רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס. The הלכה follows רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, as רב נחמן ruled.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical law for a cut that is somewhat out of the ideal place.

phrases.english: And the halacha is like Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus,
since Rav Nachman holds like him.
phrases.notes: This points back to רב נחמן's ruling earlier, about a cut from the שיפוי כובע and below.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא כְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion with a final ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, as shown by רב נחמן's practice.

steps.title: Defining the case where רבנן and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה argue
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא, in the name of רב אסי, says they argue when two-thirds was cut inside the large ring and one-third was cut out of place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רב אסי: The argument is where he cut two-thirds and then slipped out of place for one-third. רבנן hold the whole שחיטה must be in the large ring. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds that most of something counts like all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins. רב הונא pins down the exact case behind the מחלוקת in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a cut of two-thirds inside the טבעת גדולה, after which the knife slipped upward for the last third. רבנן disqualify it because they need the whole cut inside the ring. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה allows it because the majority was done properly.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute.
He moved the knife out of the proper place.
The large ring at the top of the windpipe.
Most of something counts like all of it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rav Huna said that Rav Asi said:
The dispute is where he cut two-thirds
and moved out of place for one-third,
for the Rabbis hold:
we require the entire slaughter to be in the large ring,
and Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda holds:
its majority is like its entirety.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב אַסִּי מַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic, explaining the משנה's dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is over two-thirds cut inside the ring and one-third out of place. רבנן need the whole cut inside the ring, while רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says the majority counts like the whole.

steps.title: רב הונא: When the out-of-place cut comes first, everyone agrees it is invalid
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא finishes his statement. If one-third was cut out of place first and then two-thirds were cut properly, everyone agrees the שחיטה is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he first cut one-third out of place and then cut two-thirds properly, everyone agrees it is invalid. The moment the animal's life goes out, we need the majority of the windpipe to have been cut by proper שחיטה, and here that did not happen.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא finishes his statement by giving the opposite case, where the bad cut came first. Here, he says, everyone agrees the animal is פסולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key moment is when most of the windpipe has been cut, because that is when the animal's life 'goes out.' If one-third was cut out of place first, then at the moment the majority was reached, only part of it came from proper שחיטה. So the majority was not done by שחיטה, and no one would allow it.

keyTerms.meaning: Diverted. The knife moved out of the proper slaughtering area (up toward the head).
Everyone agrees
The life (of the animal)
The majority must be cut through proper שחיטה
Invalid (the animal is not kosher-slaughtered)

phrases.english: But if he diverted the knife and cut one-third,
and then slaughtered two-thirds properly,
everyone agrees it is invalid,
because when the life goes out,
phrases.notes: The life 'goes out' once most of the windpipe has been cut.

phrases.english: we need the majority to be through slaughter, and it is not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל הִגְרִים שְׁלִישׁ, וְשָׁחַט שְׁנֵי שְׁלִישׁ – דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל פְּסוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב הונא's statement from Step 12 by giving the reverse case, where everyone agrees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If one-third was cut out of place first and two-thirds were cut properly afterward, all agree the שחיטה is invalid, since the majority was not reached through proper שחיטה.

steps.title: רב חסדא flips the case: the argument is when the bad cut comes first
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the opposite of רב הונא. The מחלוקת is in the case where one-third was cut out of place first, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה compares it to a half-damaged windpipe.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to him: On the contrary, the Master should say the reverse. The argument is when he first cut one-third out of place and then two-thirds properly. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds it is just like a windpipe that was half damaged.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא disagrees with רב הונא and switches the cases around. He says the argument is in exactly the case רב הונא called 'everyone agrees it is invalid.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Take a windpipe that is already half damaged. Cutting a bit more properly makes the שחיטה work, even though the earlier part was not cut by שחיטה. So רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says the out-of-place first third is the same: the last proper cut completes the majority. That makes this case open to argument, not something everyone agrees on.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
The opposite, the reverse
The argument, the dispute
It is just like (a comparison to another case)
A damaged windpipe

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two sages. רב הונא says the argument is when the proper two-thirds came first. רב חסדא says the argument is when the bad third came first.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said to him:
On the contrary, let the Master say the opposite:
the dispute is when he diverted and cut one-third,
and then slaughtered two-thirds,
for Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda holds
it is just like a windpipe that is half damaged.
phrases.notes: If half the windpipe was already damaged, cutting a little more properly is enough to make the שחיטה valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא: אַדְּרַבָּה, לֵימָא מָר אִיפְּכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב הונא's setup from Steps 12–13 and offers the reverse.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that everyone agrees the case of 'diverted one-third, then slaughtered two-thirds' is invalid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A half-damaged windpipe is valid once the rest is cut properly. So רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה could reasonably allow this case too, which means it is not a case where everyone agrees.

steps.title: How the Rabbis tell the two cases apart
steps.stepSummary: According to רב חסדא, רבנן reject the comparison. In the half-damaged windpipe case, the damage is in the proper slaughtering area; here the first cut was not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבנן say: there, it is the place of שחיטה. Here, it is not the place of שחיטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains, inside רב חסדא's approach, why רבנן do not accept רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the half-damaged windpipe, the damage sits in the proper slaughtering area, so the majority is still counted in the right place. Here, the first third was cut where you are not allowed to slaughter. So the majority was not reached in the מקום שחיטה, and רבנן say it is invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: The proper place on the neck for slaughtering
There (the other case)
Here (our case)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis hold:
there, it is the place of slaughter,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the half-damaged windpipe. The damage was inside the proper slaughtering area.

phrases.english: here, it is not the place of slaughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, הָתָם מָקוֹם שְׁחִיטָה, הָכָא לָאו מְקוֹם שְׁחִיטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning of רבנן against רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's comparison in Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases (location of the defect)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case of a half-damaged windpipe and the case of a first third cut out of place are the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ. The half-damaged windpipe is damaged in the מקום שחיטה, but the out-of-place cut is not in the מקום שחיטה.

steps.title: רב חסדא: When the proper two-thirds come first, everyone agrees it is valid
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא concludes that if two-thirds were cut properly first and then one-third out of place, everyone agrees the שחיטה is valid, based on the משנה 'most of one is like all of it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he slaughtered two-thirds properly and then diverted for the last third, everyone agrees it is valid. We learned in a משנה: most of one סימן is like all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא finishes his reversed version. The case רב הונא said was argued over is, for רב חסדא, one that everyone agrees is כשרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once two-thirds were cut properly, the majority of the windpipe is already done through valid שחיטה. The משנה teaches that cutting most of a סימן counts like cutting all of it. So the out-of-place last third does not matter at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Valid (properly slaughtered)
The majority of one סימן counts like the whole of it

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: the argument is when two-thirds came first, and all agree it is invalid when the bad third came first. רב חסדא: the argument is when the bad third came first, and all agree it is valid when two-thirds came first.

phrases.english: But if he slaughtered two-thirds,
and then diverted and cut one-third,
everyone agrees it is valid,
for we learned in a Mishnah:
the majority of one is like the whole of it.
phrases.notes: This משנה appears later in the מסכת. Cutting most of one סימן counts as cutting the whole סימן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל שָׁחַט שְׁנֵי שְׁלִישׁ, וְהִגְרִים שְׁלִישׁ – דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל כְּשֵׁרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב חסדא's reversed version (Steps 14–15) by giving the case where everyone agrees, the opposite of רב הונא's Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If two-thirds were cut properly first and then one-third out of place, all agree it is valid, because רובו של אחד כמוהו.

steps.title: רב יוסף questions the proof from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks רב חסדא how he knows the משנה 'most of one is like all of it' is accepted by everyone. Maybe it is only רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: Who says that the 'majority' ruling in that משנה was not taught by רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה? Maybe he is the one who taught it!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks the proof רב חסדא just brought. He suggests the משנה might reflect only one side of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said that 'everyone agrees' when two-thirds were cut properly first, because of the משנה 'רובו של אחד כמוהו'. רב יוסף says that proof only works if רבנן also accept that משנה. If only רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה taught it, רבנן might disagree, so there is no 'everyone agrees'.

keyTerms.meaning: Majority, meaning the rule that cutting most of a סימן counts as cutting all of it
Teaches it, meaning he is the author of that teaching
Perhaps, maybe

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to him:
phrases.notes: He is speaking to רב חסדא, answering the proof in step 16.

phrases.english: Who will tell us
that this 'majority' ruling there

phrases.aramaic: לָאו רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה קָתָנֵי לַהּ?
phrases.english: was not taught by Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda?

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה קָתָנֵי לַהּ!
phrases.english: Perhaps Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda taught it!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן נֵימָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof רב חסדא used in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that everyone agrees, based on the משנה 'רובו של אחד כמוהו'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה may follow only רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, so it cannot show that רבנן agree.

steps.title: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks: does every 'majority' rule in the world come from רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה? That cannot be right.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Is that to say that all the majority rulings in the world were taught by רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי argues against רב יוסף's suggestion. He says it makes no sense to pin a basic majority rule on just one sage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Majority rules show up in many places. If we say this one belongs only to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, why not say all of them do? אביי thinks רב יוסף's idea goes too far.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? A rhetorical question showing an idea is far-fetched
All the majority rules in general

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Is that to say all the majority rulings in the world

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה קָתָנֵי לְהוּ?
phrases.english: were taught by Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ כֹּל רוּבֵּי דְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back against רב יוסף's challenge in step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב יוסף's suggestion that the majority משנה belongs only to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: If one majority rule is pinned on him, every majority rule could be, which is absurd.

steps.title: רב יוסף narrows his point to slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains he does not mean every majority rule. He means only majority rules about שחיטה, because we know רבנן argue with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה there.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am talking about the majority rule of slaughter, because we have heard that they argue about it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends his challenge by making it smaller. It only applies to majority rules in שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our case, רבנן and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה already argue about a partial cut in שחיטה. So it is reasonable that a שחיטה majority rule could be his view alone. That keeps רב יוסף's question against רב חסדא alive.

keyTerms.meaning: The majority rule in slaughtering: cutting most of a סימן
We heard, we know
They argue, they disagree

phrases.english: He said to him:
I am talking about majority in slaughter,
since we have heard that they argue.
phrases.notes: 'They' means רבנן and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who argue in our case.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנָא רוּבָּא דִּשְׁחִיטָה קָאָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's objection from step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי thought רב יוסף was pinning every majority rule on רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב יוסף means only majority in שחיטה, where we already know רבנן disagree with him.
steps.whatToRemember: In the first version, רב יוסף questions whether 'רובו של אחד כמוהו' is accepted by everyone. He limits his doubt to majority in שחיטה.

steps.title: Second version: where the argument really is
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רב הונא in the name of רב אסי says the argument is when one-third was cut out of place first and then two-thirds properly. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה compares it to a half-damaged windpipe; רבנן say the damage there was in the proper slaughtering area.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some tell it another way. רב הונא said in the name of רב אסי: The argument is when he moved the knife out of place and cut one-third, and then cut two-thirds properly. רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה holds it is just like a windpipe that is half damaged. רבנן say: there, the damage was in the place of slaughter; here, it was not in the place of slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the whole discussion. In this version, רב הונא himself says what רב חסדא said in the first version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the argument is placed in the case where the bad cut came first. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה is lenient, comparing it to a half-damaged windpipe. רבנן are strict, because a half-damaged windpipe is damaged in the proper area, but here the first cut was outside it.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version of the discussion
He moved the knife up out of the proper slaughtering area
One-third
A damaged windpipe
The proper place for slaughtering on the neck

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. In this second version, רב הונא says what רב חסדא said in the first version (steps 14-16), not what רב הונא said in steps 12-13.

phrases.english: Some say it in another version:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rav Huna said in the name of Rav Asi:
The argument is where he moved the knife out of place for one-third
and then slaughtered two-thirds properly,

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר:
phrases.english: for Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Yehuda holds:
it is just like a windpipe that is half damaged,
and the Rabbis say: there, it is the place of slaughter,
here, it is not the place of slaughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא אָמְרִי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second version of the discussion that began in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument is when one-third was cut out of place first and two-thirds properly afterward: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה is lenient, רבנן are strict.

steps.title: Second version: when everyone agrees it is valid
steps.stepSummary: If two-thirds were cut properly first and then one-third out of place, everyone agrees the שחיטה is valid, because of the משנה 'most of one is like all of it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he slaughtered two-thirds and then moved the knife out of place for one-third, everyone agrees it is valid, for we learned in a משנה: most of one סימן is like all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא finishes his statement in the second version. He names the case where there is no argument at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once most of the סימן was cut properly, the שחיטה is already complete, so what happens afterward does not matter. The next step questions this proof: in this version רב חסדא asks whether the משנה is accepted by everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
Valid, kosher
Cutting most of one סימן counts as cutting all of it
One of the two pipes cut in שחיטה: the windpipe or the food pipe

steps.whatToRemember: Second version: the argument is when the bad cut came first. If two-thirds were cut properly first, everyone agrees the שחיטה is valid because of 'רובו של אחד כמוהו'.

phrases.english: But if he slaughtered two-thirds,
and then moved the knife out of place for one-third,
everyone agrees it is valid,
for we learned in a משנה:
most of one is like all of it.
phrases.notes: 'One' means one סימן, either the windpipe or the food pipe.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל שָׁחַט שְׁנֵי שְׁלִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב הונא's statement from step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When two-thirds were cut properly first, everyone agrees the שחיטה is valid, based on 'רובו של אחד כמוהו'.

steps.title: רב חסדא doubts that the majority rule is accepted by everyone
steps.stepSummary: In the second version, רב חסדא asks how we know the משנה 'most of one is like all of it' is not just the view of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא objected: Who tells us that the 'majority' rule taught there is not from רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה? Maybe he is the one who taught it!
steps.whatsHappening: In this version the roles are switched. Now רב חסדא is the one who doubts that the majority rule is a rule everyone agrees to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 said everyone agrees that two-thirds cut properly is valid, because of the משנה 'most of one is like all of it.' רב חסדא attacks that proof. If that משנה follows only רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, then רבנן might not accept it, and 'everyone agrees' falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it (a challenge to the previous statement)
A majority (here, cutting most of a סימן)
Perhaps

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a repeat of steps 17-19 by mistake. It is the same argument told in the second version, where רב חסדא asks the question, רב יוסף pushes back, and רב חסדא then narrows his point.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda objects to this:
Who will tell us
that the 'majority' taught there

phrases.aramaic: לָאו רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה קָתָנֵי לַהּ?
phrases.english: was not taught by Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda?

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה קָתָנֵי לַהּ!
phrases.english: Perhaps Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda taught it!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב חִסְדָּא: מַאן לֵימָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof used in step 21 by questioning who taught the majority משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 21 that everyone agrees, based on the משנה 'רובו של אחד כמוהו'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that משנה is only the view of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, it cannot show that רבנן agree.

steps.title: רב יוסף: not every majority rule comes from רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף pushes back: does every 'majority' rule in the world come from רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: Is that to say that all the majority rules in the world were taught by רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף rejects רב חסדא's doubt. He says it is unreasonable to pin every majority rule on one תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Majority rules show up all over the תורה. Saying each one belongs only to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה makes no sense, so רב חסדא's doubt seems to go too far.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (a question showing something is unreasonable)
In general, in the whole world

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to him:
Is that to say that all the majority rules in the world

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה קָתָנֵי לְהוּ?
phrases.english: were taught by Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ כֹּל רוּבֵּי דְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב חסדא's doubt as too broad.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the majority משנה might belong only to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would make every majority rule a one-sided opinion, which is unreasonable.

steps.title: רב חסדא limits his doubt to majority rules about slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that he means only majority rules about שחיטה, because there we know רבנן argue.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am talking about the majority rule of שחיטה, since we heard that they argue about it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא narrows his question so it no longer sounds unreasonable. He only means the majority rule in שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known argument about majority in שחיטה between רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה and רבנן. So it is possible that the שחיטה משנה about majority follows only him. The doubt about step 21 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Kosher slaughter by cutting the סימנים
They argue

phrases.english: He said to him:
I am speaking about the majority rule of slaughter,
since we have heard that they argue about it.
phrases.notes: 'They' means רבנן, who argue with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה about a windpipe cut out of place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנָא רוּבָּא דִּשְׁחִיטָה קָאָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's push-back by narrowing the challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the claim
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא seemed to say every majority rule might belong to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: He means only the majority rule in שחיטה, where a known argument exists.

steps.title: Dispute over a windpipe cut out of place, then properly, then out of place
steps.stepSummary: A new case: one-third cut out of place, one-third properly, one-third out of place. רב הונא quotes רב as saying it is valid. רב יהודה quotes רב as saying it is טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he cut a third out of place, then a third properly, then a third out of place: רב הונא said in the name of רב that it is כשרה; רב יהודה said in the name of רב that it is טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new case about cutting the windpipe in thirds and gives two opposite reports of רב's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here only the middle third was cut in the right place, so there is no majority of proper שחיטה. Even so, רב הונא reports that רב called it valid, and רב יהודה reports that רב called it טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Moved the knife and cut outside the proper slaughtering area
One-third
Valid; the animal may be eaten
Forbidden; the animal may not be eaten

phrases.english: If he cut a third out of place,
and slaughtered a third properly, and cut a third out of place –
Rav Huna says in the name of Rav: it is valid,
Rav Yehuda says in the name of Rav: it is a tereifa.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִגְרִים שְׁלִישׁ, וְשָׁחַט שְׁלִישׁ, וְהִגְרִים שְׁלִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the two-part cases in steps 20-21 to a three-part case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two conflicting reports of רב: כשרה (רב הונא) and טרפה (רב יהודה).

steps.title: The reasons behind each ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא: the animal's life went out during the proper cut. רב יהודה: we need a majority cut properly, and here there is none.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא says in the name of רב it is valid, because when the life went out, it went out through proper slaughter. רב יהודה says in the name of רב it is טרפה, because we need a majority cut by proper slaughter, and there isn't one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind each side's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא looks at what happened at the moment the animal died. It died during the proper middle cut, so the שחיטה counts. רב יהודה looks at quantity. Only one-third was cut properly, which is less than the required majority.

keyTerms.meaning: The animal's life force
Goes out, leaves
We require
There is not

phrases.english: Rav Huna says in the name of Rav: it is valid –
since when the life went out,
it went out through proper slaughter.
Rav Yehuda says in the name of Rav: it is a tereifa –
we require a majority by proper slaughter, and there isn't.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי נָפְקָא חִיּוּתָא בִּשְׁחִיטָה קָא נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for the two rulings in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא: what counts is that the life left through proper שחיטה. רב יהודה: a majority of the סימן must be cut properly.
steps.whyThisMatters: These two ways of thinking (the moment of death vs. a majority cut properly) explain why the rulings flip in the next case.

steps.title: The reverse case: proper, out of place, proper
steps.stepSummary: One-third properly, one-third out of place, one-third properly. רב יהודה quotes רב as saying it is valid. When asked, רב הונא said it is טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he cut a third properly, a third out of place, and a third properly: רב יהודה said in the name of רב that it is כשרה. People came and asked רב הונא, and he told them it is טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the order is reversed, and so are the rulings. רב יהודה permits and רב הונא forbids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two-thirds were cut properly here, so there is a majority of proper שחיטה, which fits רב יהודה's reasoning for כשרה. רב הונא's reasoning looks at the moment the life goes out, when the majority is reached. Here that happened during the out-of-place middle third, so he forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: They came and asked him
Slaughtered, cut in the proper place

phrases.aramaic: שָׁחַט שְׁלִישׁ, וְהִגְרִים שְׁלִישׁ, וְשָׁחַט שְׁלִישׁ –
phrases.english: If he slaughtered a third, cut a third out of place, and slaughtered a third –
Rav Yehuda says in the name of Rav: it is valid.
They came and asked Rav Huna,
he said to them: it is a tereifa.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁחַט שְׁלִישׁ, וְהִגְרִים שְׁלִישׁ, וְשָׁחַט שְׁלִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the opposite arrangement of thirds, with the rulings reversed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה (quoting רב): כשרה. רב הונא (his own answer): טרפה.

steps.title: רב יהודה is upset that רב הונא keeps ruling the opposite way
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה heard and was upset: where I forbid he permits, and where I permit he forbids!
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה heard and was upset. He said: I declare it טרפה and he declares it valid; I declare it valid and he declares it טרפה!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה complains that in both cases רב הונא ruled the exact opposite of him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case (out of place, proper, out of place) רב יהודה forbade and רב הונא permitted. In the second case (proper, out of place, proper) it flipped. רב יהודה, who heard this case directly from רב, is bothered that רב הונא contradicted him.

keyTerms.meaning: He became upset, was annoyed
I declare it forbidden
I declare it valid

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda heard and was upset,
he said: I declare it a tereifa and he declares it valid,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets; the words in square brackets are the corrected wording. The meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: I declare it valid and he declares it a tereifa!
phrases.notes: The first half is the earlier case from step 25; this half is the case in step 27.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע רַב יְהוּדָה אִיקְּפַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב יהודה reacts to רב הונא's ruling in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling of טרפה in the case of proper, out of place, proper.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יהודה had a ruling from רב, and רב הונא contradicted it in both cases.

steps.title: רב הונא admits רב יהודה was right to be upset
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא agrees: רב יהודה heard it from רב and I did not. Also, there is a majority cut by proper שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: He is right to be upset. First, he heard it from רב, and I did not hear it. And besides, there is a majority cut by proper slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא accepts the complaint and gives two reasons why רב יהודה's ruling of כשרה should stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, a ruling heard directly from רב outweighs רב הונא's own reasoning. Second, on the facts, two-thirds were cut properly, so there is a majority of proper שחיטה. That makes it look like רב הונא is backing away from his טרפה ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Properly, rightly
First... and also (listing two reasons)
He heard it (as a tradition)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: שַׁפִּיר קָא מִיקְּפַד,
phrases.english: Rav Huna said: He is right to be upset,

phrases.aramaic: חֲדָא – אִיהוּ שְׁמִיעַ לֵיהּ מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַב,
phrases.english: first – he heard it from Rav,
and I did not hear it,
and furthermore – there is a majority cut by proper slaughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: שַׁפִּיר קָא מִיקְּפַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב הונא responds to רב יהודה's complaint by agreeing with him.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב הונא's ruling of טרפה can stand against רב יהודה's report from רב.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No: רב יהודה has a direct tradition from רב, and there is a majority of proper שחיטה.

steps.title: רב חסדא tells רב הונא not to back down
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא tells רב הונא: do not retract your ruling. His reason comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to him: Do not take back your ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא pushes back against רב הונא's retraction. This line sets up an explanation that the גמרא gives next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא had just accepted that the case is כשרה. רב חסדא rejects that retraction and holds that the original ruling of טרפה was correct. His reason comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not take back your words

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said to him:
Do not retract,

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֶּהְדַּר בָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב הונא's retraction in step 29.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב הונא's decision to give up his ruling of טרפה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not stated yet; the reason comes next in the גמרא.
